faq.q: Can I show a closet before and after?
faq.a: Yes, when the after state is something the product really does. Describe both states in plain language, and do not invent a result the rack cannot produce.

faq.q: Will furniture show up at the right size?
faq.a: The scale in the picture can drift. Put the true dimensions in the listing. You can still mention a size in the scene, such as a 24-inch side table next to an armchair.

faq.q: Does this work for sofas and beds?
faq.a: Yes, if the photo shows the whole piece, legs included, and you name a room large enough to hold it. A missing leg or handle cannot be invented later.

faq.q: Can I start from a photo on a white background?
faq.a: Yes. Keep the entire product in frame, including legs, handles, and cords. The scene can only use what that photo already shows.

faq.q: Can I make a short cleaning demo?
faq.a: Yes. Show one mess the viewer can see, hold the camera steady, and let the product make a single pass.

faq.q: What should I describe in the scene?
faq.a: Name the room, the furniture nearby, the light, and the one action shoppers need to see. Keep exact dimensions and materials in the listing text.

faq.q: Can I run these clips as paid ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloads carry no watermark, so a room clip can go straight into a paid ad.

faq.q: Do I need a studio or a hired model?
faq.a: No. Choose an AI avatar instead of booking a model or a set. A clip can include a voice, a voiceover, captions, a music track, and a script. If that clip fails, the credits return.

faq.q: Can a product link lead to more than one version?
faq.a: Yes. Paste the listing, or let your shop software send it through the API. Ask for the lamp off in one version and on in the next, then trim both in the editor before you export.
